Data Quality Dimensions

A practical framework for deciding whether information is fit for operations, reporting, analytics and AI.

Browse all 14 slides

Quality is defined by the decision

This presentation turns broad data-quality concerns into measurable dimensions, executable checks and accountable ownership. It connects source systems and pipelines with the decisions and automated actions that depend on them.

A dataset can pass one dimension and fail another. The framework therefore combines individual measures, use-case thresholds, monitoring and upstream remediation.

The seven core dimensions

DimensionQuestionExample measure
AccuracyDoes it reflect reality?Correct values ÷ values checked
CompletenessIs required data present?Non-missing required values ÷ expected required values
ConsistencyDo facts agree across systems?Matching records ÷ records compared
TimelinessIs data available when needed?Arrival lag or freshness relative to a use-case threshold
ValidityDoes data follow defined rules?Passing values ÷ tested values
UniquenessAre unintended duplicates absent?Duplicate records ÷ total records; lower is better
IntegrityAre relationships valid?Valid relationships ÷ total relationships

Why data quality dimensions matter A single bad field can propagate across reporting, automation, and AI. Data Quality Dimensions Source Systems Data Pipeline Trusted Assets Analytics & AI Decisions & Actions WHAT GOES WRONG Pipeline failures Missing rows, schema changes, stale loads Bad metrics Wrong KPIs, duplicate counts, broken joins AI risk Incorrect retrieval, biased models, unsafe agent actions Dimensions convert “the data looks wrong” into specific, measurable controls: accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, validity, uniqueness, and integrity. 02

Seven Measurable Dimensions

Open hosted slide

The core framework: seven measurable dimensions Each dimension answers a different business question. Data Quality Dimensions FIT FOR PURPOSE Accuracy Is it correct? Completeness Is required data present? Consistency Does it agree everywhere? Timeliness Is it current enough? Validity Does it follow rules? Uniqueness Is each entity once? Beyond the core: dimensions that matter at enterprise scale Mature programs extend the framework based on domain risk and usage. Data Quality Dimensions Enterprise-scale quality dimensions Conformity Standard formats, codes, naming conventions Precision Correct level of measurement detail Granularity Right aggregation level for analysis Reliability Stable, dependable delivery over time Accessibility Available to authorized users and systems Lineage Source-to-consumption traceability The right dimensions depend on context: financial transactions, customer master data, product catalog, RAG knowledge base, and ML feature store each need different thresholds. 08

Executable Data Quality Rules

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Convert dimensions into executable rules Quality improves when business expectations become automated checks. Data Quality Dimensions Dimension Executable rule template Completeness `Customer_ID`, `Email`, `Signup_Date` must not be NULL. Validity `Country_Code` must be a valid ISO 3166 code. Consistency CRM status must match billing status for active accounts. Integrity Every `Order.Customer_ID` must exist in `Customer.Customer_ID`. Timeliness Transactions must arrive in the fraud platform within 60 seconds. Uniqueness `Tax_ID` must be unique across active customer records. Rule failure should create an operational signal: severity, owner, lineage, failed records, and remediation path. 09

Scoring and Hard Thresholds

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Scoring: useful, but guardrails matter more Composite scores help trend quality, but critical dimensions need hard thresholds. Data Quality Dimensions WEIGHTED SCORE EXAMPLE Accuracy (30%) 98% Completeness (20%) 96% Consistency (15%) 99% Freshness (10%) 95% Validity (10%) 99.5% Uniqueness (5%) 99% Integrity (10%) 99.9% Overall DQ Score ≈ 97.8% But do not let averages hide critical failures. Hard guardrails Financial transactions: completeness = 100% Customer master: duplicate rate < 0.1% Fraud data: freshness < 60 seconds Principle Score trends are useful. Blocking thresholds protect the business. 10

Data Quality for ML, RAG and AI Agents

Open hosted slide

Data quality for ML, RAG, and AI agents AI systems amplify the strengths and weaknesses of their data. Data Quality Dimensions Training Data Feature Pipeline ML Model RAG Docs Retrieval AI Answer COMMON QUALITY FAILURE MODES Incorrect labels → bad predictions Missing attributes → biased or weak models Training-serving skew → production drift Obsolete RAG docs → outdated answers Duplicate chunks → retrieval imbalance Bad metadata → wrong permissions/context Incorrect operational data → unsafe agent action Stale CRM status → wrong outreach Bad entity resolution → wrong customer For AI, quality dimensions become control knobs: source reliability, freshness, lineage, access control, and confidence must travel with the data. 12

Ownership and Accountability

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Ownership model: quality is a business process Technology detects failures; accountable owners prevent recurrence. Data Quality Dimensions Create Forms, APIs, source apps Data producer Ingest Validation, reconciliation Data engineer Transform Tests, joins, aggregates Data engineer Publish Contracts, documentation Data product owner Consume Dashboards, ML, agents Business / AI owner OPERATING MODEL Data owner Business accountability for domain quality. Data steward Definitions, standards, thresholds, exceptions. Engineering owner Pipelines, tests, alerts, remediation automation. Consumers Report defects and define fit-for-use needs. Best practice: fix the process that creates the defect, not just the downstream record. 13

Slide 14 of 14

Implementation Roadmap

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Implementation roadmap A pragmatic sequence for moving from ad hoc cleanup to governed data products. Data Quality Dimensions 1 Identify critical assets Customer, transactions, product, finance, ML features, RAG corpora 2 Define fit-for-use expectations Consumers, decisions, thresholds, regulatory obligations 3 Translate into rules Dimensions → metrics → executable checks → owners 4 Automate and alert Run in pipelines; classify severity; route failures with lineage 5 Remediate upstream Fix source process; track trends; prevent recurrence Closing principle The goal is not perfect data. The goal is data that is sufficiently accurate, complete, consistent, current, valid, unique, and trustworthy for the decision or automated action. 14

Reading the scoring example

The percentages on slide 10 are illustrative. Applying the displayed weights to the displayed values gives 97.84%, rounded to 97.8%. A high average does not override a failed critical threshold. The duplicate-rate metric on slide 7 is lower-is-better, whereas the uniqueness score used in a composite must have a clearly defined higher-is-better interpretation.

Frequently asked questions

What are the seven core data quality dimensions?

The presentation identifies accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, validity, uniqueness and integrity. Each tests a different aspect of whether data is fit for its intended use.

How do accuracy and validity differ?

Accuracy asks whether a value reflects reality. Validity checks whether it follows defined formats, ranges and rules. A value can pass validation and still be incorrect.

How should duplicate records be measured?

The deck shows duplicate records divided by total records. This is a duplicate rate, where lower is better; it should not be treated as a higher-is-better uniqueness score without conversion.

Why are composite scores not enough?

A weighted average can hide a failure in a critical dimension. The deck pairs score trends with hard thresholds defined for the use case.

Why does data quality matter for AI?

The slides connect incorrect labels, missing attributes, stale documents, duplicate chunks and faulty metadata with failures in ML predictions, RAG answers and agent actions.
